# `m.indices.snapshots`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The current state of each index: its level, its session so far, and its status.

```python
m.indices.snapshots(symbols, *, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Methods | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `LastUpdated` |
| `sort` | `ticker` |
| `filters` | `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Indices with the `I:` prefix, or `dm.ALL` for every index. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `sort` | `"ticker"`, the one field Massive sorts by. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. A watchlist's `fetch()` caps every request instead. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"ticker_gte": "I:N"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Indices Snapshot (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Indices Basic | Not included |
| Indices Starter | 15-minute delayed |
| Indices Advanced | Real-time |
| Indices Business | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "Ticker of asset queried." | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Value` | double | Value of Index. | REST |
| `Error` | String | The error while looking for this ticker. | REST |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. | REST |
| `MarketStatus` | String | The market status for the market that trades this ticker. | REST |
| `Message` | String | The error message while looking for this ticker. | REST |
| `SessionOpen` | double | The open value for the index of the day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionHigh` | double | The highest value for the index of the day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionLow` | double | The lowest value for the index of the day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionClose` | double | The closing value for the index of the day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionChange` | double | The value of the change for the index from the previous trading day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionChangePercent` | double | The percent of the change for the index from the previous trading day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `SessionPreviousClose` | double | The closing value for the index of previous trading day. From the `session` object: Trading session metrics, detailing change percentages and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. | REST |
| `Name` | String | Name of Index. | REST |
| `Timeframe` | String | The time relevance of the data. | REST |
| `Type` | String | The indices market. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
